plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying relative to my value. Since my value is $19, I will bid exactly $19 to ensure optimal expected profit.

This is a second-price auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies, since shading down only risks losing profitable wins without reducing what I'd pay upon winning. My value is $44, so I will bid exactly that amount to ensure I capture any positive surplus whenever the second-highest bid is below my value.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own), so bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable and never overpay relative to my valuation. Shading my bid down doesn't help since I don't pay my own bid when I win. I will bid exactly my value of $43 to maximize expected profit.
